content.text: {"stops":[{"poi_id":"p9","kind":"activity","must_do_id":"m3","note":"The old stones of Pisac hold stories, and the terraces catch Inti (the sun) just right."}]}

{"stops":[{"poi_id":"p8","kind":"activity","must_do_id":null,"note":"Wander the Inca galleries and let the old stones whisper their stories."},{"poi_id":"p7","kind":"activity","must_do_id":null,"note":"A sweet little workshop where cacao gets the farewell it deserves."}]}

{"stops":[{"poi_id":"p2","kind":"activity","must_do_id":"m2","note":"The Inca stonework here still holds its shape after all these centuries, and Inti (the sun) used to bounce off sheets of gold."},{"poi_id":"p1","kind":"activity","must_do_id":null,"note":"A fine square for watching Cusco wake up around you, with the cathedral keeping an eye on everyone."},{"poi_id":"p12","kind":"activity","must_do_id":null,"note":"The white statue looks over the red rooftops, and the valley opens up like a story waiting to be told."},{"poi_id":"p14","kind":"meal","must_do_id":null,"note":"A warm, wood-panelled spot where the vegetarian plates are as generous as the welcome."}]}

{"stops":[{"poi_id":"p3","kind":"activity","must_do_id":"m1","note":"Giant Inca stones with a view over the red-tiled roofs; the zigzag walls feel like a sleeping puma."},{"poi_id":"p4","kind":"activity","must_do_id":"m4","note":"A riot of fruit, flowers and woven colour; follow your nose to the juice stalls."},{"poi_id":"p16","kind":"meal","must_do_id":null,"note":"Andean comfort food done with care, and the vegetarian plates are proper feasts."},{"poi_id":"p5","kind":"activity","must_do_id":null,"note":"Gold-leaf altars and a painting of a very local Last Supper; quiet and cool inside."},{"poi_id":"p6","kind":"activity","must_do_id":null,"note":"Cobbled lanes, tiny workshops and balconies spilling with geraniums; easy to wander slowly."},{"poi_id":"p18","kind":"meal","must_do_id":null,"note":"Wood-fired pizza and a cosy courtyard; a relaxed end to the day."}]}
A warm Cusco hello, Inca stones, the Sacred Valley, and a sweet goodbye — all under Inti (the sun).
